verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 6.7, last paragraph: 'Orbit graphs and projections are exported as plain TikZ coordinates.' SPEC.md 4.0 [D] Share and export: 'LaTeX export (dynkin-diagrams and TikZ, section 6.7) arrives in phase 6.' SPEC 4 T8 ('the graph of all positions reachable from all ones by legal play, drawn in layers') and T12 ('the orbit drawn in layers with edges coloured by node'). Read together, these support the finding's expected.
verdicts.evidence: Read SPEC 6.7 whole. The sentence has no label and no qualifier ('may', 'where ... allows'). The [S] label belongs to the compile sentence, not to this one. Section 4.0 is [D], but its LaTeX bullet points to 6.7, and 6.7 assigns orbit graphs to TikZ. Phases: T8 is phase 3, T12 is phase 5, and LaTeX export is phase 6 (4.0; 9.1 row 6 'LaTeX export'). All three are due at G6. Records at f07eec6: DECISIONS.md 'P6-A5: ToolFrame, the prop latexForExport and the default export' is a builder's design: a tool without the prop exports the board's \dynkin. 'P6-A5: TikZ export in the tools (request)' asks for T2 and T10 'and if wanted T8 and T6'. 'MERGE: P6 stage 6.1, P6-A5, and stage 6.1b, P6-A2' assigns only T2 and T10, as 'needed for the owner's G6 compile of one file of each kind'. 'MERGE: P6-tikz ...' wires T2 (tikz-graph) and T10 (tikz-points) and leaves to the owner only edge colours, labels and rise lines. No record exempts T8 or T12 from 6.7, and no section 10 default applies. The P6-A5 plan line 135 says 'T02 ... and T10 ... at least'. git grep at f07eec6 finds latexForExport passed only by T02OrbitGarden.svelte and T10GeometryStudio.svelte. reports/gate-G6.md (d59af4a, gate commit f07eec6 confirmed) checks only the three sample forms and lists no open item on T8 or T12. This is the first round of phase 6, so there is no earlier merge report. The known-and-decided list names only 'edge colours and labels in the TikZ forms'.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 failed, because 6.7 states the TikZ export of orbit graphs with no permissive clause; R2 failed, because T8's and T12's figures are orbit graphs drawn in layers (SPEC 4) and 6.7 governs them; R3 failed, because LaTeX is phase 6 and the tools are phases 3 and 5, all due at G6; R4 does not apply, since no oracle value is involved; R5 failed, because the default \dynkin export is a builder's choice outside the 6.7 text, not an owner's answer or section 10 default, and MERGE scoped T2 and T10 only for the G6 compile samples without exempting the others; R6 failed, because neither gate-G6.md nor an earlier round records it. Severity stays major (a stated behaviour missing).

verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 2.4(a) [D]: 'The number on node i is the amount by which a mutation would lower city i. ... This sentence is the bridge between the two views and must appear, with the same wording, wherever the two views are shown together [D].' SPEC 1.7: 'the two views of a board are called Populations (the mutation game; roots) and Numbers (the numbers game; weights)'. SPEC 4 T14: 'highest roots and their numbers'.
verdicts.evidence: The [D] sentence is an obligation ('must appear ... wherever'). It has no exception for static or reference pages. By SPEC 1.7 the two views are Populations (roots) and Numbers. AtlasSheet.astro at f07eec6 prints θ (a root population) beside 'its numbers are Cθ', the highest short root 'with the numbers', the paragraph 'A population lists the coefficients of a root ...; the numbers of a position are its Dynkin labels', and 'The translation a=Cp sends the populations onto ...'. So the Atlas puts both coordinate systems of one root side by side, which T14 itself requires. Bridge records in DECISIONS.md: P1-A5, P1-A8, P1-A9, P3-A4, P3-A8, P3-A9 'no linked view' (M5, about T1's linked view only) and the P6-A8 glossary row 10. None exempts the Atlas. The P6-A4 entries (lines 3990 to 4039) and 'MERGE: P6-A4 reviewed; rulings' never mention the sentence. Earlier rounds' coverage lines (round-p4 RT-10, round-p5 RT-10 and RT-08) apply the sentence wherever both views appear, including prose pages such as /not-quiver-mutation/, and excuse it only where a page shows one view (T10, T11, T12, M8). The known-and-decided list has no bridge item. The P6-A4 plan has no bridge item. reports/gate-G6.md has no open item.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 failed, because 2.4(a) [D] has no qualifier that lets a page showing a population and its numbers together leave the sentence out; R2 failed, because the finding quotes the sentence exactly and the Atlas does show both views by 1.7's definition; R3 failed, because T14 is phase 6, at G6; R4 does not apply; R5 failed, because the [D] text requires the sentence and leaving it out is a departure, not a choice within the text, with no owner ruling; R6 failed, because no earlier ruling or open item covers the Atlas. A stated message is missing, so the severity stays major.

verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 8.4 bullet 1: 'Define every term on first use and link later uses to a glossary entry'. SPEC 9.2: for a lesson '(M10 is reference pages and has none); it follows the writing rules of section 8.4'. SPEC 3 M10. The passage supports the finding's expected.
verdicts.evidence: 9.2 exempts M10 only from predictions and challenges ('M10 is reference pages and has none'). The same sentence then says it 'follows the writing rules of section 8.4', and 8.4 bullet 1 has no qualifier. 8.4 is not [D], and no section 10 default touches it (D14 covers house style 'as proposed'). Records: 'MERGE: P6 stage 6.3, P6-A7 (M9) and P6-A8 (M10 and the glossary)' sends to P6-terms 'the same later-use rule as a shared spec over every lesson M0 to M9 and the reference pages'. 'P6-terms: the shared spec glossary-later-uses.spec.ts' and 'MERGE: P6-terms ...' name the 15 routes (M0 to M9 and history, confusions, open-problem, not-quiver-mutation, about). None of these says M10 is exempt. They only leave it out of the scope. P6-A8's anatomy entry (no beats, no Seen box, no sources) says nothing about glossary links. The known-and-decided list holds 'one markup for a defined term distinct from bold' and 'M10's question', neither of which covers links on later uses. I read m10-atlas.mdx at f07eec6 and counted 'board' in its glossary sense 8 times in the figcaption and hub items, 9 with the question. 'finite type' appears 2 times, 'numbers game' 2 times (glossary item and credit line) and 'Kostant's game' 2 times (history item and credit line). The file imports no Term helper. Nothing in the record contradicts the finding's observed.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 failed, because 8.4 bullet 1 is unqualified and 9.2 binds M10 to 8.4 while exempting it only from predictions and challenges; R2 failed, because the finding reads 8.4 and 9.2 correctly; R3 failed, because M10 is phase 6, at G6; R4 does not apply; R5 failed, because 8.4 is not [D], there is no section 10 default, and MERGE's P6-terms scope leaves M10 out without a recorded exemption; R6 failed, because nothing is on record (first phase 6 round, no gate-G6 open item). A broken prose rule of 8.4 is major, so no adjustment.

verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 9.3 bullet 4: 'When an open decision of section 10 blocks work, take the default, and add a line to DECISIONS.md with the date and the reason.' SPEC 10 D10 (default 'keep separate; note in both that on simple graphs the rule and C=2I-A agree') and D12 (default 'English'). The passage supports the finding for D12; for D10 it is ambiguous.
verdicts.evidence: grep -E '\bD1[02]\b|MutationGraph|English|Languages|research-software' on DECISIONS.md at f07eec6 finds no entry naming D10 or D12. The only hit for the language is line 331, '2026-10-10 P0-A5: Base.astro created; the stylesheet link', which records `<html lang="en">` with the reason 'the instruction, section 5.12' but does not say a section 10 default was taken. Every other default has a named line (for example 'P0-A1: D18 default used', 'P6-A6: D5, D11, D13, D14, D16, D17 ...'). gate-G6.md says every fragment is folded (1265 headings), so no fragment holds a missing record. The 9.3 qualifier 'blocks work' is the one possible refutation (R1). For D12 it fails: every page's lang attribute needs the language, so the site uses D12's answer from phase 0. For D10 it is arguable: the lens's own file (RT-10 section 2 item 7) says D10 'needs no code' and is 'relied on by no build phase', and its check from phase 6 is a plan reading. The site contains no MutationGraph note (git grep at f07eec6). The known-and-decided list and the MERGE entries hold no D10 or D12 ruling. RT-VERIFY 5.4: 'A section 10 default without a record is not R5.' 9.1 G0's owner part names D1, D3, D4 and D17 only, which gives no exemption.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 holds at most for the D10 half, through 9.3's 'blocks work' (the lens concedes D10 needs no code), but the D12 default (English, lang="en" on every page since phase 0) is used, and line 331 of P0-A5 records the attribute, not the default with its reason, so the cause stands; R2 failed, because the finding quotes 9.3 whole; R3 failed, because D12 is used from phase 0; R4 does not apply; R5 failed, because a default without a record is not R5 (RT-VERIFY 5.4); R6 failed, because nothing is on record. The ambiguity of 'blocks work' for D10 is for the owner. A missing required DECISIONS.md entry is major.

verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 4.0 [D] Test hooks: 'Every node button carries data-node (its label), data-board (populations or numbers, which matters in the linked view), data-value (the value shown, as decimal text, or as p/q for a fraction) and data-can-act (true or false).' SPEC 2.15: 'So the shadows carry a mutation game of their own, on the restricted board ...'. The passage supports the finding for the restricted board.
verdicts.evidence: 4.0 is [D] at its heading, and its Test hooks sentence names exactly two data-board values. DECISIONS.md '2026-10-25 P6-A3: the data-out names and the extra hooks (deviation to confirm)' records data-board="decoration" with data-value the colour, and data-board="restricted' with the stated reason '4.0 names only populations and numbers; a third value keeps the Challenge component's reading of the game board's populations clean'. The builder itself calls this a deviation. Neither 'MERGE: P6 stage 6.2, P6-A3' (rulings 1 to 3: C2 drawing, whereToRun, data-moves) nor 'MERGE: P6-A3 reviewed; rulings' nor 'MERGE: P6-A3 and P6-A4 repaired after review' rules on it. The review's 'confirmed ... the hooks' refers, in P6-A3-review.json, to 'the four 4.0 hooks are on every node button', that is, presence, not values. A partial refutation exists for the paint buttons: the decoration shows neither populations nor numbers, and the P6-A3 plan (line 188) itself makes them 'a hook outside 4.0's list'. That does not reach the restricted board, whose values are shadow coordinates. By 2.15 these carry a mutation game, so 4.0's 'populations' applies, and the third value departs from the [D] text for convenience. RT-VERIFY 5.4: 'R5 holds for a choice within the [D] text, never for a departure from it.' Lines read at f07eec6: DecorationDiagram.svelte:138 and RestrictedBoardView.svelte:92 carry the values the finding names.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 failed, because 4.0 lists only populations and numbers with no 'may', and 2.15 makes the restricted board's values populations of a mutation game; R2 failed, because the finding quotes 4.0 exactly, and the reading that 4.0 cannot apply holds only for the paint buttons, which leaves the restricted-board part standing; R3 failed, because T13 is phase 6; R4 does not apply; R5 failed, because P6-A3 logged a departure 'to confirm' that MERGE never ruled on, and a departure from [D] text is not R5; R6 failed, because nothing is on record. Severity: the rubric of RED-TEAM-COMMON 4 lists 'a hook' wrong under major.
